blocker.summary: The r399 allocator double-issue is RESOLVED (r413/r414/r415). r416/r417 established boot now progresses past sub_821D5F48 and the per-frame loop runs sustained; 'generated entry terminated its own thread' is r277's designed clean-shutdown, not a stall. r418/r419 found presented_frames=0 is pre-existing dead-code wiring (r292, unrelated to r399) and confirmed a real, standalone-reproducible process hang: on the r414-fixed binary the process never exits on its own after printing its final diagnostic (not specific to AC6_NATIVE_VD_TRACE). r420 root-caused this WITHOUT a live attach, by reading source: VulkanDevice::~VulkanDevice() (native_vulkan_device.cpp:228) is a correct, complete RAII destructor (vkDeviceWaitIdle/vkDestroyDevice/vkDestroyInstance) -- this REFUTES r419's working hypothesis that Vulkan teardown was missing. The real cause: NativeRuntime::shutdown() (native_runtime.cpp:184) calls native_guest_threads_stop_and_join() FIRST, before anything else, and that function (native_guest_threads.cpp) does an UNCONDITIONAL, TIMEOUT-LESS thread.join() on every ExCreateThread-spawned guest worker thread registered via native_guest_threads_register (the only caller: the generated ExCreateThread stub, tools/materialize_native_import_stubs.py:1056). The clean-shutdown mechanism (r277/r417: generated wait stubs check stop_requested() and throw GuestThreadTerminated) only works if the targeted thread happens to be parked inside one of those specific wait stubs at the exact moment shutdown is requested -- if even one registered worker thread is instead doing real PPC execution or blocked in some other host call that doesn't poll the flag, .join() on it blocks forever, shutdown() never returns, main() never reaches the point where `runtime` (and its owned unique_ptr<VulkanDevice>) goes out of scope, and the driver's own thread pool ([vkcf]/[vkrt]/[vkps], observed by r419) stays alive as a downstream consequence -- not because Vulkan teardown itself is broken. This also explains why the hang was never seen before r414: boot never previously reached a state with enough sustained, realistic worker-thread activity for one to plausibly be caught outside a wait stub at shutdown time. The GPU poller thread (NativeGuestVdService::poll_loop, native_guest_vd.cpp:181) is spawned via a bare detached std::thread, NOT registered via native_guest_threads_register, so it is not the direct cause of this specific join hang, though it shares the same underlying gap (nothing ever asks it to stop either). Named for r421: identify precisely which registered worker thread is stuck and why (a bounded diagnostic trace addition, or a live gdb -p attach if the user explicitly authorizes working around this sandbox's ptrace_scope restriction) before designing a fix -- not a blind timeout on .join(), which would risk masking a real leaked/wedged thread rather than fixing the underlying issue. The standing uncommitted-tree situation (r239+, over the 2026-09-02 mass deletion) remains the user's decision, untouched -- reports and named tool scripts for r413-r420 were committed individually, the broader tree state was not.
